methodological_questions: Can the closest pre-absence initiation-profile teammate be shown to be the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells or cases are needed to test a ranking of teammates by usage gain?
What are the risks of deriving play types and initiator labels from play-by-play outcomes?
How should the pre-absence profile be defined and validated?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type replacement similarity vs absorb/cascade. Mean similarity was +0.863 for ABSORBED vs +0.848 for CASCADE; Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19, which the record calls wrong-signed. Verdict null, failure type B_powered_null, with limitation LIM:label_or_classification_error. Sample and power were NOT_RECORDED.

Season stability of top suppressors and negative teammate pairs. Only 2/30 stars (7%) met the 75% same-top-suppressor stability rule. Failure type B_powered_null with LIM:small_sample; 30 stars x 4 seasons, minimum n=20 per cell.

Offensive-identity resilience. Connector absence displaced team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence: paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, n=96 matched pairs. The vs-terminal comparison was n=25. Risks recorded: MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. Its outcome is team identity, not teammate usage gain.

On-ball defensive scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH). Confident label rates were 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL); switches_on was unpopulated. Failure type A_unanswerable with LABEL_ERROR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Superstar sequential suppression. PUTBACK was the top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g. D. Mitchell d=-0.294, n_after=95). No multiplicity correction; n_after was 30-95 for several cells against thousands of baseline possessions. Risk: DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type. Several star-lineup PPP gaps were reported, e.g. Jokic vs MIN -0.385 (n=59). No placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Failure mechanism E_unclear.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap for initiators: pooled gap +0.427 PPP (38 BEST vs 94 AVOID players at n>=10). Only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers. Limitation LIM:small_sample; risk SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID H2 PPP gaps (exploratory). 78 players with at least 5 rows per tier; several large gaps alongside reverse gaps. No multiplicity or clustered test; failure mechanism A_unanswerable, risk PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

Player BEST/AVOID tier tendency in H2 trigger games. Team AVOID% ranged 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC); player samples were 10-178 possessions. Descriptive only; no outcome test; failure mechanism E_unclear.

Route entropy: whether shaper presence expands the play repertoire. Non-focal entropy change was -0.0455 (n_ts=80) with no CI reported. The paper reads it as rebalancing rather than expansion. Verdict null, failure type E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type replacement similarity to separate absorption from cascade when a player sits (the closest prior analogue to a similar-profile-teammate test).
failed_approaches.why: Similarity did not separate the outcomes (ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848), the sign was wrong, and the record flags label or classification error. The similarity was almost always findable, so the measure did not discriminate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating each star's top sequential suppressor as stable across seasons, and reading teammate X->Y negative premiums as reliable.
failed_approaches.why: Only 2/30 stars met the stability rule. Cells were small (min n=20), which the record reads as underpowered for stable rankings.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball coverage from NBA matchup/PBP fields.
failed_approaches.why: Label rates were too low (14.9% and 3.3%), and switches_on was not populated, so the label was not usable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing star suppression to lineup and forced-play-type contrasts without placebo control.
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking top opponent suppressors per star across many cells without correction.
failed_approaches.why: No multiplicity correction and small n_after cells against large baseline counts; drift was flagged as a risk.

evidence_establishes: Close analogues of this question have not produced a clean positive result. The most similar record (FAM:SF-CHT-052) found no separation between absorbed and cascaded outcomes by profile similarity, with the sign reversed.
Play-type labels and initiator attributions derived from play-by-play have had reliability problems in this project (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-CHT-052).
Small per-player or per-cell samples have repeatedly yielded unstable top-ranked teammates or suppressors (FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF-APPS-036, FAM:SF-APPA-048).

Usage-matched comparisons with a placebo-style control (FAM:SF-APPS-088) have produced a positive result for a related but different outcome (team identity displacement), which supports the matching approach.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types. No retrieved record tests this ranking for absences.
Any estimate of the number of absences needed for the ranking test. Retrieved records do not record power for this design.
Whether the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data, with 11 cases, supports the test. Retrieved records do not cover this data version.
The validity of the pre-absence profile definition (closest profile, minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes). No validation is recorded for any retrieved family.
own_inferences: The unit that matters is the absence case, not the spell. The 148 spells are nested in 11 cases, so the effective sample is about 11 for between-player comparisons. Spells within a case are not independent.
With 11 cases and a ranking over several teammates, the chance of a clean test at useful power is very low. Even a large true effect would be hard to distinguish from noise.

Matching or ranking on pre-absence profile can be contaminated by the same usage that defines the profile (regression to the mean). The teammate who most resembles the absent player may already be a high-usage player whose gains are capped by ceiling effects.
The question's wording (largest gainer) makes a single ranking claim, so the test is sensitive to which teammates are included and how ties are handled.
uncertainties: Sample sizes and power for this exact question are not recorded in any retrieved family.
Whether the 11 cases are all distinct players, and how many teammates each case offers as candidates.
Whether the derived initiator and play-type labels have been validated against manual or tracking data for this data version.
Whether the 2025-26 playoffs and regular-season partial files change the case count before the cutoff date.
How the primary play types are defined for each absent player (threshold, pre-absence window).

historical_effect.explanation: The closest prior analogue (FAM:SF-CHT-052) found no separation by profile similarity, with the sign reversed and label-error limits. Combined with the small-sample and label-reliability failures (FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF-APPS-058), this shifted the decision from proceed to do_not_proceed as posed. The matched-control design in FAM:SF-APPS-088 informs the minimum viable test, but it does not establish this question.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 absence cases are available. A ranking over several teammates per case cannot reach useful power at this size, even with 148 spells.
Primary play-type possessions per absent player and per teammate may be sparse in short spells, which makes the per-play-type gains noisy.
Initiator and play-type labels are derived from play-by-play outcomes, and the closest related family records label or classification error (FAM:SF-CHT-052, FAM:SF-APPS-058).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the closest-profile teammate as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types. FAM:SF-CHT-052 is the closest analogue and found no separation by profile similarity, with a wrong-signed result and label-error limits. FAM:SF-APPA-058 showed weak stability of top ranked teammates or suppressors. FAM:SF-APPS-088 used a usage-matched control and found a supported effect for team identity displacement, which is a different outcome. The question is therefore only partly addressed by earlier work.

risks.text: 11 absence cases is too few to rank teammates reliably. Spell-level counts (148) overstate the effective sample because spells are clustered within cases.
The pre-absence profile (initiation share, minutes, same-position minutes) may have low test-retest reliability across seasons, so the closest-profile teammate may be unstable.
Play types and initiator labels are derived from the same play-by-play outcomes used to measure gains, so the outcome and the label are not independent.
Play-type and initiator classification errors are documented in related families and could bias which teammate is classified as the gainer.
Absences are often selected after a player's usage peak or injury-related dip, so pre-absence profiles may regress toward the mean and mimic a gain for similar teammates.
Teammate gain may reflect lineup, minutes, coach changes, or role shifts that coincide with the absence, not profile similarity.
Many teammates gain a little after any absence. Without a base rate for gains, the largest-gainer claim is weak even when true.
Ranking many teammates across several play types invites chance winners; without placebo absences the top gainer may be an artifact of ranking.
Several profile definitions (closest profile, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) and several play types create many possible rankings.
Usage and roster context shift across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooled gains may mix different eras.

design.estimand: Per absence case, the difference in the change in primary-play-type usage between the closest-profile teammate and the mean of other eligible teammates, compared with the same difference in matched non-absence windows. The primary test asks whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types more often than chance.
design.unit: Absence case (player-absence event). Spells are nested within cases and are used only as within-case repeats.
design.sample: 11 absence cases from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs files, using the 148 spells as repeated measures within case. The minimum viable test requires more absence cases than 11. Prior to analysis, the case count must be stated and locked.
design.power: Not achievable at 11 cases for a ranking over several teammates. Power must be computed by simulation over the case count before any analysis. Until then the design is descriptive only.
design.controls: Pre-absence baseline usage and minutes for each teammate; position and same-position minutes; matched non-absence windows for each absent player (placebo windows); team and season fixed effects; a permutation test that reassigns the closest-profile label within team-season; a measure of profile reliability across pre-absence windows.
design.falsification: Run the same ranking on placebo windows where no absence occurred. If the closest-profile teammate ranks as the largest gainer at a similar rate in placebo windows, the result is an artifact of the ranking or of regression to the mean.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary profile definition and one primary play-type set. Correct any secondary profile or play-type comparisons (e.g. Holm or Bonferroni) and report them as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only if (a) at least the pre-specified minimum number of absence cases is available, (b) the closest-profile teammate ranks as the largest gainer more often than the placebo-window rate with a CI excluding chance, and (c) the result is stable across profile definitions. If not met, report as inconclusive or untestable and do not claim the ranking.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs per-game files as listed. The 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are partial before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21 respectively, so the cutoff date must be fixed and the data frozen before analysis.

methodological_questions: Can the closest pre-absence initiation-profile teammate be shown to be the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells are needed to test a ranking of teammates by usage gain?
What are the risks of deriving play types and initiator labels from play-by-play outcomes?
How should the pre-absence profile be defined and validated?

You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
